aliases: prime-keyed exact log and gcd sieve (log-sieve retrieval)
AERM exact relation store (D2, G v1)
plain_what: A fact is written once under an exact address and read back exactly, instead of being smeared across weights or found by fuzzy similarity. Addresses are built from prime numbers, so the same words name the same slot. A newer value replaces the old one, the old one stays recoverable, and a missing fact can say I do not know.
how_it_works: Three built forms. (1) Exact log plus sieve: every user turn is logged as word atoms, each word with a prime from a registry table. A clause's address is its square-free set of content primes plus ordered pairs (n-lets). A query admits a clause when gcd(query, clause) > 1, computed as a sorted merge of factor lists. Ranking is separate: most shared primes, then latest occurrence, then ordered-pair match. A record is evicted only when its ring slot was overwritten. (2) AERM store (G v1): learned heads tag tokens as entity, relation, value or other; an integer store maps (entity, relation) -> value, keeps the previous distinct value and a version counter, and a read returns None, Hit, Absent or Evicted for the current and previous register. The prime-route variant keys by the semiprime p_a*p_b of two atoms, which names the unordered pair exactly by unique factorization; the value is routed through the expert so direction survives. (3) Product-key memory: the query splits into two halves, each scored against S sub-keys; the top k per side give k^2 candidate slots scored by the sum; the best k are read from an S^2-row value table. Sub-keys are learned or fixed to the 120 unit icosians or 240 E8 roots. The built form mixes rows with softmax weights.
geometry: Prime atoms and square-free semiprimes (unique factorization), ordered n-lets, gcd divisibility; optional fixed sub-key codebooks from the 600-cell (120 unit icosians, H4) and the 240 E8 roots; Lorentz (hyperboloid) distance as an optional sub-key score.

status_reason: Every trained form that was tested failed its bar or broke a rule: learned read triggers failed held-out phrasing (docs/integration/g1-always-on-read-result-2026-09-28.md); the product-key form uses softmax weights and scored 19/40 against a 27/40 bar (docs/labs/addressed-memory-2026-10-10/README.md). The address-as-read form was never built. Not on the D32 run plan; the integer exact store itself is rule-compatible.
reopen_conditions: Build the address as the READ, not an MLP replacement: add memory fields to the dialogue settings and train the store and read in from the start (D22 section 5(c) order, never executed), 2-3 seeds, frozen panel of at least 80 rows; brief bar is at least +8/40 over 19/40 with BPB within 0.01.
Run the cheap serving-time address oracle first (supply the true slot address) to bound the gain before any training.

Re-register as a D37 offline-float sheet or a D32 discrete sheet with a softmax-free value mix (rank table or hard select), a separately scanned module, an integer export and a reported export gap; needs a fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT and owner release.

Provide an integer read kernel (gcd or sorted-merge admission plus table value read) in uor-r4-integer; today integer serving refuses product-key memory (docs/labs/native-address-port-2026-10-11/README.md) and has no gcd.

Report address-formation accuracy (tagging or query-key) separately from read accuracy, since 77.7 percent of held-out failures were query-entity tagging (docs/integration/g1-decomposition-result-2026-09-29.md).

rule_compat.D11: Exact store, sorted-merge admission and shift-subtract gcd are table and integer operations by design. No served form exists: uor-r4-integer has no gcd, and integer serving refuses product-key memory (native-address-port record, 3 memory_shape tests pin the refusal).
rule_compat.D23: The exact log, sieve and AERM store contain no softmax. The product-key built form mixes rows with softmax weights (stack_memory.rs docs), and the learned tag and trigger heads trained with cross-entropy: those parts are banned.
rule_compat.D30: The store and sieve use no matmul. The tested forms sit inside the dense float stack (query maps, tag heads), so they are not D30-clean as built.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Integer exact store matches the D32 integer shape. Learned tagger or query map would be float under D37 with an integer export and reported gap; the discrete crate has no memory store yet. No hold released.

open_questions: Where does the exact store sit in the D32 discrete model: as a Relation/Route read target over retained structure, or as a separate store behind the object-store crate?
Retrieval caused only 2.2 percent of failing rows in the era-22 chat panel (eras.md, #1708): is memory the binding constraint on the M1 headline at all?
Can address formation (query entity and relation tagging) be made exact enough, e.g. by prime registry lookup of repeated words, that no learned tagger is needed for verbatim keys?
Should the key be entity prime times attribute prime written when the fact is stated, with a learned gate from the exact hit into the output, or copy the value token directly?
A learned gate from the store's exact hit versus copying the value directly (brief open question 2).
How are abstention and eviction scored fairly when a fact was legitimately evicted from a bounded ring?

related: pointer-key: copies the value token the address names; the pointer found the source but not the slot
read-binding: teaches an attention read which stated value belongs to the question, the learned alternative to an exact address
object-store: exact byte storage of source material beneath the model, no addressing of facts
e8-orbit-memory: the E8-addressed product-key variant of this memory, replacing an MLP
relation-read: the D34 reranker reads retained structure; exact edges would come from this store
admission: the measured ceiling on what any read can reach (2,201 of 14,287 targets at Q1)
prime-zeta-codebook: supplies the prime registry the sieve and semiprime keys depend on
route-read and flock-read: similarity-free alternatives that read by address or small kept sets
figure_ideas: A conversation scrolling past a row of numbered slots: each stated fact writes a tile whose label is a product of two primes; a correction stacks a new version on the old tile; a question lights the gcd match and the right version, while an unwritten key shows 'Absent' and an overwritten ring slot shows 'Evicted'.

Bar chart of the D2/G v1 cliff for one seed: in-distribution 1.000, held-out templates 0.000-0.158, held-out with gold register 1.000, beside the stacked failure causes (query-entity tag 77.7 percent, zero eviction, zero wrong stored value).

A 256 by 256 grid of value slots: two half-queries each pick a few rows and columns, the crossings light up as k-squared candidates, and only the best k cells (a token reads 32 rows of 65,536) are read.
